##### Random network NPSEM and graph generators

A random network NPSEM (RNNPSEM, @def-npsem-ne) has two kinds of equation. *Structural* equations represent constructs measured on each observational unit; *relational* equations represent the causal processes linking constructs across observational units. A graph generator is an array of relational equations, one for each pair of distinct nodes, giving the entries of a random network graph. In a general random network, nothing is assumed about how the relational error terms depend on each other: they need only be independent of the structural variables. In a bipartite random network (@def-bipartite-npsem-ie), each person's row of the adjacency matrix, their network weights, is one variable in their observational unit, so the network becomes person-level data and single-world independence holds row by row: a person's links to different places may share a disturbance.
